# AI agents and tools

Applies when the change touches: an agent, tool calling, MCP, or A2A. Every role loads this pack for the steps it works in, on top of its own playbook. The test commands below are best practices the gate runs: put them in the Spec's `[[tests.commands]]`, so a red one blocks the merge. Name the pack in the Spec's Context; it does not count against a Task's `skills`.

## Checklist by loop step

| Step | Item |
| --- | --- |
| Entry (`aidd next`) | A new tool, MCP server, or permission is major: name the irreversible actions it can take. |
| Specify | Least privilege per tool: an allow-list of actions, scopes, and hosts; human approval for irreversible actions; a kill switch. |
| Specify | Trust boundaries drawn: what the agent reads is untrusted, what it may do is a tool (OWASP Agentic ASI01, ASI04). |
| Implement | Sandbox tool execution; validate tool arguments against schemas; no secret in the agent's context; every tool call traced with the OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions. |
| Review | Trace an injected instruction from each input to each tool and show it is blocked or waits for a human. |
| Ship | Tool-call error rate, unusual action volume, and cost are the observe signals; a spike rolls back. |

## Test commands

| Command | Proves | How |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tool-permission tests | every call outside the allow-list is denied | unit tests on the tool layer |
| Injection scenarios (emerging) | an instruction in each untrusted input cannot reach a tool | scripted red-team evals (garak, promptfoo) |
| MCP server audit | transport auth, origin validation, no token passthrough | the MCP security best-practices checklist, scripted where possible |
| Loop and cost guards | max steps, max tokens, and timeouts stop a runaway | unit tests |
| Trace coverage | every tool call emits a span | an OpenTelemetry test exporter in the tests |

## Keep it current

A standard marked emerging is a draft, a first edition, or a young practice: apply it only when the change clearly needs it, and say so in the Spec. A standard checked more than a year ago is stale: `aidd eval standards` lists it, and the loop contract's research-first rule applies. When the change needs a standard this pack lacks, look up the authoritative source, record the edition in the Spec's Context, and propose the update to the aidd project's roles registry (`schemas/roles.json` in the aidd repository) as an improvement.
